text:
maria: Heads-up — we're planning to change SIEM export retention for dev logs from 90d -> 30d starting next Monday. Anyone see major concerns?

jong: Why dev only? production stays 365?

maria: yes prod stays 365, we still keep audit indices (auth, admin actions) at 180d. dev spike this quarter bumped costs.

priya: How are we handling KMS wrapping for the exported S3 bucket? Need envelope encryption and explicit CMK usage.

maria: plan is to use a dedicated CMK `kms-redwood-exports` with key policy limited to exporter role + security-ops. Rotation enabled. Exporter will use SSE-KMS when writing to S3.

alex: Who approves the RBAC change to allow the exporter role to call `kms:Encrypt`/`kms:Decrypt`? Do we do an IAM ticket + security review?

dave: I'll file the IAM change in JIRA and tag `security-review` + `compliance`. Need the exact scope to avoid overly broad permissions.

sec_ops_bot: [alert] export-failure detected 03:12 UTC — exporter retried 3x, queued for backoff.

maria: Noting: for forensic needs we may need masked/unmasked copies. Prefer masking + longer metadata retention rather than full unmasked exports.

priya: Agreed. Also add a DLP/gating check in the export pipeline: scan for PII before allowlist export to S3. If DLP hits, fail the export and notify SOC.

maria: I'll add a pre-export DLP step. Quick command example for exporter to use SSE-KMS:

maria: ```
aws s3 cp /tmp/export.json s3://redwood-siem-exports/2026-03-10/export.json --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```

alex: For the IAM change, scope to the single CMK ARN and include condition `kms:ViaService` where appropriate. Only allow `kms:Encrypt` for the exporter; `kms:Decrypt` only for the SOC decrypt-proxy role.

dave: Filed ticket ENG-4231 with proposed policy and proof-of-concept. Linked this thread and set reviewers `@sec_lead`.

priya: Another ask: give SOC analysts ephemeral read-only access via a proxy role with JIT (24h) sessions rather than long-lived keys. That reduces standing permissions.

maria: Yes — plan is JIT with 24h sessions issued via the access-request service (approval workflow). We'll document the approval steps and audit logs.

jong: Do we need to update any compliance artifacts for customers who have longer retention SLAs?

maria: Prod retention SLA unchanged. We'll add a note to the compliance pack that dev exports are truncated to 30d unless explicitly requested for incident investigations. Those will be handled via a documented JIT export request with approvals.

priya: Also: run a DLP sample run on last month's exports before rolling this to catch edge cases.

maria: Good call — I'll kick off a sample DLP sweep tonight and post results here.

alex: +1 on limiting `kms:Decrypt` to SOC proxy and on the JIT flow.

dave: tagging the IAM reviewers and scheduling a quick design review tomorrow 10:30 PST.

maria: Target rollout Monday 09:00 PST. If there are blockers, ping me ASAP. :rocket:
